source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: A student asked whether writing several detailed paragraphs of instruction into a skill risks the same context problems as an overloaded chat conversation. What was the answer?

options.text: Yes, so skill instructions should always be kept to one paragraph or less
options.feedback: No length limit was set. The answer turned on where instructions sit relative to the task, not on capping how many paragraphs they run to.

options.text: No, because a skill's instructions sit right next to the work they govern
options.feedback: The instructions arrive attached to the specific task at hand rather than competing for attention against a long, wandering chat history, which is what makes an overloaded conversation lose the thread in the first place.

options.text: Yes, but only for skills that also include scripts or other runnable code
options.feedback: The answer carved out no exception for code-bearing skills. Instructions sitting next to the relevant task holds whether or not the skill bundles scripts.

options.text: No, because skill instructions are processed by a completely separate model from chat
options.feedback: Nothing suggests a second model handles skill instructions. The same model reads them -- just without the competing clutter of a long conversation around them.
